items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: discussion over the phone with Joe that George Buck might be interested in doing an album

ctx.x: Yes, the 1966 Manasses, first of all Manasses Jazz Festival. So he came up and there had been some discussion over the phone with Joe that George Buck might be interested in doing an album. I wasn't sure I wanted to make an album for him that time and, you know, what did I have to work with.
But anyway they insisted and I got stranded down in North Carolina because we had this blizzard in New York and I couldn't get home so they more or less --

items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: Aunt Joe, I guess they practically lived in church most of the time.

ctx.x: Oh, yes, they were Black churches, yes, oh, yes. Now, my uncle -- my mother's brother who lived in Ranken, now they were quite church goers, you know. My Uncle Paul, he sang in the choir and Aunt Joe, I guess they practically lived in church most of the time. I remember that -- well, I attended a lot of services at the church where Uncle Paul sang. He sang not only in the choir, but there was a trio that he sang with. That I recall. I suppose that was one of the reasons why he was in church most of the time,…
